code_label: Long-term returns often remain non-Gaussian
text_span: their distributions often exhibit a high level of asymmetry and bimodality
rationale: States the central empirical phenomenon the paper addresses.

code_label: Quantum walk can generate asymmetric bimodal distributions
text_span: the occurrence of interference effects, which allows for the generation of bimodal and asymmetric probability distributions
rationale: Summarizes the proposed modeling mechanism.

code_label: Quantum walk complements short-term models
text_span: this analysis complements traditional short-term models and offers opportunities to more accurately describe the probabilistic structure underlying long-term financial decisions
rationale: States the intended contribution and use case.

code_label: Classical random walk was the first financial time-series model
text_span: The first model to describe the dynamics of financial time series was developed by Bachelier in 1900
rationale: Provides historical framing for the modeling approach.

code_label: Short-term return distributions can often be power-law fitted
text_span: The distributions of returns defined over time scales ranging from 15 seconds to a few days can often be adequately fitted with power laws
rationale: Describes established behavior at short horizons.

code_label: Long-horizon return distributions are underexplored
text_span: Return distributions defined over large time scales of the order of months and years are a rather underexplored topic in the literature
rationale: Motivates the paper’s focus on long-term returns.

code_label: Gaussian convergence is commonly assumed
text_span: It is commonly assumed that for increasing time scales, return distributions converge toward a Gaussian distribution
rationale: Identifies the classical benchmark the paper challenges.

code_label: Observed long-horizon shapes are often asymmetric or bimodal
text_span: one frequently observes non-Gaussian shapes, often exhibiting a high level of asymmetry and even bimodality
rationale: States the empirical pattern the paper later documents.

code_label: Quantum walk is an extension of classical diffusion
text_span: it represents one of the simplest possible extensions of a classical diffusion process incorporating quantum interference effects
rationale: Positions the model as a minimal extension of classical diffusion.

code_label: Decoherence collapses quantum walk to classical random walk
text_span: Introducing decoherence into the quantum walk causes it to collapse to a classical random walk
rationale: Explains the relationship between the quantum and classical models.

code_label: Unitary quantum walks are deterministic
text_span: unitary quantum walks yield fully deterministic probability distributions
rationale: Justifies the choice to exclude decoherence in the analysis.

code_label: Study targets assets with pronounced asymmetry or bimodality
text_span: we focus on financial assets with long-term return distributions that exhibit a clear level of asymmetry or bimodality
rationale: Defines the empirical sample selection focus.

code_label: Large-scale analysis uses 31 assets over up to 30 years
text_span: We analyzed the time series of the opening price of 31 financial assets, including stocks and funds
locator: 3. Identifying asymmetry and bimodality in return distributions
rationale: States the dataset size and asset types.

code_label: Large time scales begin at 100 trading days
text_span: We refer to time scales ∆t as “large” from 100 trading days onwards
locator: 3. Identifying asymmetry and bimodality in return distributions
rationale: Defines the threshold used for long-term analysis.

code_label: Bimodality emerges at longer horizons
text_span: For ∆t > 50 trading days, the P∆t(g) in Fig. 1 display clear bimodality
locator: 3. Identifying asymmetry and bimodality in return distributions
rationale: Reports the observed transition in distribution shape.

locator: 3. Identifying asymmetry and bimodality in return distributions

code_label: Bimodality measure emphasizes equal peaks and separation
text_span: it should adopt a large value if the two peaks are equally high, and if the probability distribution substantially drops between them
locator: 3. Identifying asymmetry and bimodality in return distributions
rationale: Explains the intended behavior of the bimodality metric.

code_label: Asymmetry quantified by skewness
text_span: The level of asymmetry in a probability distribution can be quantified by the skewness
locator: 3. Identifying asymmetry and bimodality in return distributions
rationale: States the statistic used to measure asymmetry.

code_label: Long-horizon distributions remain strongly skewed
text_span: The distributions have a persistent level of asymmetry |γ1| ≳0.5 across different time scales ∆t
locator: 3. Identifying asymmetry and bimodality in return distributions
rationale: Reports the empirical skewness finding.

code_label: Classical Gaussian models fail at long horizons
text_span: These models fail to adequately capture pronounced asymmetry and bimodality in long-term return distributions
locator: 3. Identifying asymmetry and bimodality in return distributions
rationale: States the inadequacy of classical models for the observed data.

code_label: Quantum walk parameters are fitted to empirical returns
text_span: determine the value of the quantum walk parameters (η, θ, ϕ, ω) that yield the best fit to the empirical return distributions
rationale: Describes the main fitting objective.

code_label: Number of time steps fixed to reduce complexity
text_span: n is set to 100
rationale: Specifies a key modeling choice.

code_label: Fixed n mainly changes width not shape
text_span: Only the width of the Pj(n) of Eq. (6) is effectively affected by altering n
rationale: Justifies fixing the number of steps.

code_label: Quantum walk peaks are smoothed by aggregation
text_span: we aggregate each three consecutive positions j with non-zero probability in the quantum walk distribution into one single point
rationale: Describes a smoothing step used before fitting.

code_label: Fit quality measured by mean absolute error
text_span: The goodness of fit is quantified by the mean absolute error (MAE)
rationale: Identifies the primary fit metric.

code_label: Optimization uses steepest-ascent hill climbing
text_span: The search for the parameters (η, θ, ϕ, ω) that minimize the MAE is performed using steepest-ascent hill climbing
rationale: Specifies the optimization algorithm.

code_label: Decoherence excluded because approaches are non-unique
text_span: there is no unique way of introducing decoherence effects into the quantum walk algorithm
rationale: States a methodological caveat for excluding decoherence.

code_label: Decoherence can erase distinctive quantum features
text_span: Even at relatively low decoherence rates, the resulting distributions resemble classical ones and the distinctive features of quantum walk distributions are lost
rationale: Explains a limitation of decoherent variants.

code_label: Quantum walk fits capture overall behavior better than Gaussian
text_span: they capture the overall behavior of the distributions noticeably better than a Gaussian distribution
rationale: Summarizes the comparative performance of the model.

code_label: Fixed-n fits overestimate peaks and truncate tails
text_span: The quantum walk fits tend to overestimate the height of the peaks, and sharply fall to nearly zero beyond them
rationale: States a specific shortcoming of the initial fits.

code_label: Initial position can represent drift
text_span: The location of the initial position |j = 0⟩ of the quantum walk ... can be associated with the general drift term
rationale: Links a model component to a financial interpretation.

code_label: Asymmetric distributions often need little drift
text_span: If the initial position is situated at g ≈0, the drift term can be neglected (µ ≈0)
rationale: Reports an empirical/modeling observation for asymmetric cases.

code_label: Bimodality reflects competing driving forces
text_span: the algorithm can accommodate the dynamics of two competing driving forces modeled by the quantum coin
rationale: Provides the paper’s interpretation of bimodal behavior.

code_label: Long-term losses and gains are important for risk analysis
text_span: providing a good quantitative estimate of the pronounced negative tails of the empirical distributions in Fig. 7 and the negative bumps of the distributions in Fig. 6 is essential
rationale: Highlights why accurate tail and bump modeling matters.

code_label: Sampling n from a normal distribution improves fits
text_span: We explore the effect of smoothing the parameter n to resolve these discrepancies and substantially improve the quality of the quantum walk fits
rationale: Describes the refinement that improves fit quality.

code_label: Averaging over random n reduces peak overestimation
text_span: This modification effectively addresses the two issues previously noted
rationale: Summarizes the effect of the revised fitting procedure.

code_label: Quantum walk outperforms Gaussian in most cases
text_span: except for the cases of ARI and NVG, the MAE of the quantum walk fit is lower than for the Gaussian fit
rationale: Reports the main comparative fit result.

code_label: Quantum walk better for bimodal distributions by KS statistic
text_span: across all bimodal distributions, the KS statistic is consistently lower for the quantum walk fit compared to the Gaussian fit
rationale: Reports a stronger fit for bimodal cases.

code_label: Parameter space shows clustering by distribution type
text_span: The bimodal and asymmetric return distributions occupy different regions in the coin parameter space
rationale: Describes a structural pattern in fitted parameters.

code_label: Further work should extend data and refine fitting
text_span: In future work, the analysis can be extended to larger data sets, and more refined fitting strategies can be explored to further improve the quality of the quantum walk fits
rationale: States explicit future research directions.

code_label: Perfect characterization is inherently challenging at two-year horizons
text_span: achieving a perfect characterization of the return distributions is inherently challenging
rationale: States a broad limitation of the approach.

code_label: Decoherence may help model short-term returns
text_span: by including decoherence effects, one can generate asymmetric probability distributions with heavier tails than a Gaussian distribution
rationale: Identifies a possible extension for future modeling.
